name: btc-shakeout-before-breakout-v1
rule: H1 (user): before BTC makes a new N-bar high it first makes a new N-bar low. Definition: for N in (15m: 2 bars=30m, 4 bars=1h); event = bar i closes a new N-bar high (high_i > max high of prior N bars). Condition = within the prior N bars a bar made a new N-bar low. Compare P(event | condition) vs P(event | not condition) and vs base rate. Pre-registered 2026-10-19T04:00Z before running on Twelve Data BTC/USD 15m (~50 days).

result.as_stated: FAILS. A new N-bar low (bar close basis) in the prior N bars makes a new N-bar high LESS likely: lift 0.70 (30m), 0.61 (1h), 0.58 (2h); mirror image identical, i.e. short-term momentum.
result.sweep_variant: HOLDS at 30m only: wick below the prior 2-bar low with the close above the prior close -> new 2-bar high within 30m 68% (n=486) vs 53% any bar vs 34% after a new low that closes down. No edge at 1h/2h (60%/53% vs 59%/60%).
result.verdict: Rewrite the rule as a sweep-and-reclaim at the 15-30 minute scale; the close direction is what matters.

name: btc-range-edge-magnet-v1
rule: H2 (user): when BTC sits within 1.0% of its 24h low (or high) for >= 12 consecutive 15m bars (3h) without touching it, and is still making small new 1h lows (highs), the 24h low (high) is broken within the next 6h. Measure P(break within 6h | setup) vs P(break within 6h | within 1% of edge for only 1-2 bars) and vs unconditional P(24h low broken in next 6h). Pre-registered 2026-10-19T04:00Z.

result.highs_1pct: HOLDS: hover within 1% of 24h high for 3h without touching + fresh 1h highs -> break within 6h 49% (n=71) vs 27% unconditional, 19% brief visits; within 12h 65% (n=46) vs 36%.
result.lows_1pct: WEAKER: break within 6h 35% (n=77) vs 22% unconditional; within 12h 47% (n=51) vs 32%.
result.at_2pct: no edge (23% vs 22% lows; 29% vs 27% highs).
result.verdict: Supported at the 1% band, strongest at highs, 1.3-1.9x base rate. "Almost definitely" is too strong: most setups still do not break within 6h.

name: btc-patterns-5m-10m-v1
rule: Re-run of shakeout and range-edge tests on Twelve Data BTC/USD 5m (5000 bars, 17.4 days, Oct 1-19) and 10m (paired 5m). Same definitions as the 15m tests.

result.shakeout_as_stated: FAILS at every window: a bar-close new low in the prior 10/15/30/60 min lowers the odds of a new high (lift 0.48-0.78).
result.sweep: 5m bars: wick below prior 10m low + close up -> new 10m high within 10m 63% (n=476) vs 53% any bar, 35% plain new low. 15m 59% vs 55%. 30m 52% vs 58% (gone). 10m bars: 10m sweep 66% (n=346) vs 46% any bar, 29% plain; 30m 59% vs 55%; 60m 57% vs 61% (gone).
result.range_edge_highs: 5m: hover 3h -> break 6h 45% (n=20) vs 23% any bar, 3% brief; 12h 53% vs 32%. 10m: 41% vs 23%; 12h 53% vs 32%. Consistent with 15m result.
result.range_edge_lows: 5m: 38% (n=26) vs 25%; 10m: 28% (n=25) vs 26% (no edge). Low-side effect is small and unstable; sample is 2.5 weeks.
result.verdict: Sweep-and-reclaim is a 10-15 minute phenomenon, decaying by 30 min. Range-edge magnet is robust at highs across 5/10/15m, weak at lows.

name: btc-reclaim-taxonomy-v1
rule: Responding to the Oct 21 master critique. Classes on breach of prior N-bar low: S_strong (close > previous close), S_level (close >= breached low but <= previous close), S_accept (close < breached low); non-breach G (close up) / R. Primary outcome: fixed target = high of the N bars before the signal exceeded within H bars. Primary contrast: S_strong vs G, Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio over distance-to-target/ATR14 quintiles, UTC-day block bootstrap 95% CI. Secondary: next-open to close-at-H forward return (bps), rolling-target rate for reconciliation with the earlier 59-68% figures. Data: Twelve Data BTC/USD 5m Aug 10-Oct 22 2026, 10m/15m resampled. Configs = the six in the critique table.

result.verdict: Sweep adds no edge after distance matching: MH OR strong-sweep vs green 0.76-0.99 across six configs (10m case significantly < 1). Old 59-68% reproduced exactly (rolling target). Forward returns -1 to +4 bps for all classes vs 40-76 bps round-trip fees. Demoted to entry geometry.

name: alt-recovery-event-study-1h-v1

Targets (step 2): coin log return minus BTC log return over 6h/24h/72h, entry at next 1h open, minus 0.40% round-trip maker cost (0.76% taker as stress). Evaluation: per-event cross-sectional Spearman rank IC per feature, averaged; chronological split first 60% of events = discovery, last 40% = holdout; a feature counts only if holdout mean IC has the same sign as discovery and |t| >= 2 across holdout events. name: multi-target-panel-baseline-v1
registered_at: 2026-10-24T04:42Z (before any model fit or outcome viewed)
data: Kraken daily OHLCV (COMP, SOL, BTC from 2024-11-03; HBAR from 2025-07-10); Twelve Data 1h OHLC snapshot (no volume) 2025-08-31..2026-10-22; Kraken 4h OHLCV 2026-06-26..; Kraken Futures hourly funding from 2025-10-15.

targets.range_widen: (high-low)/open over next window > same over previous window
targets.vol_up: coin dollar volume over next window > previous window (volume datasets only)
targets.shape: one of trend_up, trend_down, breakout_up, breakdown, failed_breakout, range (rules fixed in code before fitting)

features: point-in-time only: coin and BTC returns over 1/3/7/30 bars, range position 24h/7d, drawdown from 30-bar high, realized vol and its change, volume ratio vs 20-bar mean (where volume exists), coin-BTC rolling correlation and its change (Yae & Tian), rolling beta, BTC drop state, day of week, hour of day (hourly), funding level and change (where available)
method: Per coin x target x horizon: chronological split, first 70% train / last 30% holdout, untouched until final fit. Models: base rate, persistence, L2 logistic (multinomial for shape) with standardization fit on train only. Decision points non-overlapping within each horizon for evaluation.
primary: Brier skill score vs base rate on holdout (log-loss skill for shape); a target is 'predictable' if skill > 0 and block-bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0. Input importance = holdout permutation importance, reported only for predictable targets.
multiple_testing: 3 coins x ~7 targets x 2-3 horizons ~ 50 looks; report all, Holm-adjusted
result: 138 coin x target x horizon looks; 36 beat the base rate on holdout, 22 after Holm. Direction (abs and vs BTC): 1/42 (none after Holm). New 7-day high: 10/21 (8 Holm); new low: 16/21 (9 Holm); range widening 3/21; volume rising 3/12; shape 3/21. Input weight share across predictable targets: 7-day range position 21.5%, volume ratio 16.6%, 24h range position 15.0%, volume trend 5.1%, realized vol 3.6%. name: kama-efficiency-panel-input-v1
source: MarketLab 1.2 (owner upload): Kaufman efficiency ratio and KAMA(10,2,30)
question: Do path-efficiency inputs improve the live panel's out-of-sample probabilities?
data: Kraken 4h and daily OHLCV pulled 24 Oct 2026 for the 15 live-panel coins plus BTC (the same pull used to set C=0.01).
features_added: efficiency ratio over 10 bars; close/KAMA - 1; KAMA 3-bar slope; efficiency ratio over 30 bars
method: Per coin x chart x horizon x target: chronological 70/30 split, train rows purged by the horizon before the cut, median impute and standardization fit on train, L2 logistic C=0.01. Baseline = live panel inputs; extended = baseline + added inputs. Compare pooled holdout Brier (sum over coins).
primary: Change in pooled Brier skill (extended minus baseline) per chart x horizon x target, and the number of coins where the extended model has lower Brier.
decision_rule: Adopt into the live model only if pooled skill improves in at least 10 of the 16 proven-target cells (new_high, new_low, range_widen, vol_up x 2 horizons x 2 charts) and no proven cell loses more than 0.01 skill. Direction and shape are reported but do not count.
result: ADOPT (10 of 16 proven cells improved; worst -0.0054). Gains concentrated in 4h-ahead new high (+0.018 skill, 12/15 coins) and new low (+0.029, 14/15); 4h 24h-ahead new high/low +0.006/+0.009; daily changes within +/-0.006. Direction unchanged (still below base). Live model is now panel-logit-v2. Artifact: research/recovery_lab/results/2026-10-24_kama_efficiency/ertest.json

name: btc-stocks-correlation-panel-input-v1

features_added: QQQ day d is known from 21:00 UTC on d. Per QQQ trading day: coin log return between consecutive QQQ closes using the coin's last closed candle at each close time. Inputs at each bar: correlation of the last 30 paired returns; that minus the preceding 30; QQQ 5-day log return. Forward-filled to bars between US closes.
method: Same as kama-efficiency-panel-input-v1: per coin x chart x horizon x target, purged chronological 70/30, L2 logistic C=0.01, baseline = current live inputs (panel-logit-v2), extended = baseline + added inputs; pooled holdout Brier.
decision_rule: Adopt only if pooled skill improves in at least 10 of the 16 proven-target cells and no proven cell loses more than 0.01 skill. Direction and shape reported, not counted.
result: REJECT (2 of 16 proven cells improved; worst -0.041, 4h 24h-ahead new high). Every 4h cell except range_widen got worse; direction got worse too. Disclosure: a first run accidentally read a different Twelve Data file (not QQQ); it was discarded, and the reported run uses the QQQ series. Caveat: on the daily chart the coin price at each US close is the last closed daily candle (up to 21h earlier), which dilutes the correlation (SOL 0.24 daily vs 0.59 on 4h); the 4h version is aligned within an hour and still hurt. Not added to the live model. Artifact: research/recovery_lab/results/2026-10-24_qqq_correlation/

name: laggard-intraday-recovery-v1
question: Does an intraday recovery in a coin that has been lagging BTC predict that it beats BTC over the next day, after costs and against matched baselines?
signal: On 15m bars, at close t, all of: (1) prior weakness: coin 30-day return minus BTC 30-day return <= -10 points; (2) relative strength: coin minus BTC return > 0 over each of the last 1, 2 and 4 bars (15m, 30m, 1h); (3) volume: USD volume of the last 4 bars >= 1.5x the mean 4-bar USD volume over the 96 bars before them (the prior 24h); (4) range: (close - 24h low)/(24h high - 24h low) >= 0.60, using the trailing 96 bars including t, and higher than the same measure 4 bars earlier; (5) persistence: conditions 1-4 true at both t-1 and t. Signal at t.
background_condition: Condition (1) alone (the coin is a laggard).
episode_reset: After an entry for coin c, no new entry for c until 24h have passed and conditions 2-4 have been false on 4 consecutive bars.
holding: Primary 24h; secondary 72h (reported, not used for the decision).
data: Kraken public Trades endpoint (full history, paged by 'since'), rebuilt into 15m and 1h OHLCV bars for every USD-quoted pair, 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-28. USD volume per bar = sum over trades of price x base quantity (all pairs are USD-quoted, so no FX conversion). Bars with no trades carry the previous close and zero volume.
universe: Point-in-time. At each decision time t a pair is eligible only if, using data before t: it has traded for at least 45 days, and its median daily USD volume over the prior 30 days is at least $1M. Excluded: stablecoins, fiat pairs, wrapped or staked BTC/ETH, tokenized gold. Pairs delisted later stay in while they traded.
execution: Signal evaluated at a bar close. Entry at the open of the next bar of the signal's timeframe. Exit at the open of the bar that starts exactly the holding period after entry. BTC leg uses the same timestamps. Outcome = coin log return minus BTC log return, in percentage points.
episodes: One entry per signal episode per coin; rule-specific reset conditions below.
costs: Primary: 0.8% round trip charged to the coin leg (explicit assumption covering fees plus slippage). Sensitivity: 1.2% and 2.0%. No cost on the BTC leg (outcome is relative).
splits: Chronological by entry time: development first 50%, validation next 20%, holdout last 30%. 72-hour embargo at each boundary: episodes whose entry-to-exit window crosses a boundary are dropped. Thresholds are frozen in this entry; no tuning on any split. Development is used only to verify code correctness.
inference: 95% confidence intervals by moving-block bootstrap over calendar days, block length 3 days, 10,000 resamples. Each resample takes whole days with every coin's episodes in them, which covers overlapping holding periods and coins moving together.
baselines: (a) Random-entry, same coin: for each episode (coin c, entry time e), 20 entry times drawn uniformly from bars within +/-3.5 days of e where c is eligible and meets the rule's background condition, excluding bars within 24h of any actual episode for c; same execution, holding period and costs; the episode's baseline is the mean of the 20. (b) Equal-weight cohort at the same time: at each episode's entry time, an equal-weight portfolio of every eligible coin meeting the rule's background condition, with costs charged on every leg. (c) Holding BTC: 0 excess, no cost.
decision_rule: Supported only if, on the holdout with at least 30 episodes: mean excess after the 0.8% cost is above 0 with the bootstrap 95% CI lower bound above 0; the mean difference vs baseline (a) and vs baseline (b) each has a 95% CI lower bound above 0; and mean excess stays above 0 at the 1.2% cost. Otherwise not supported. Either way the live monitor and holdings are unchanged; a supported result is research evidence only and needs a separate decision before any use.
known_bias: Kraken-only universe. Trade history for some delisted pairs may be missing (survivorship). The 0.8% cost is assumed, not measured per pair. One test of each rule; results describe Jan 2025 to Oct 2026 only.
authority: Research only. Not a live signal, not a Lagebild input, cannot open trades or change size.

question: Using only information available at the time, after BTC dips, do altcoins bought at the next open beat holding BTC over the following days, after costs?
data: Kraken public daily OHLC (UTC days), last 720 days available at run time (about Nov 2024 to Oct 2026), for BTC and every USD-quoted pair. Daily USD volume = Kraken daily VWAP x base volume.
universe: Point-in-time: at event day t a pair is eligible if, using data before t, it had traded at least 45 days and its median daily USD volume over the prior 30 days was at least $1M. Same exclusions as the other two tests.
trigger: At a completed daily close t: BTC close <= 0.94 x the highest BTC daily close over days t-7 to t-1. No condition on what happens after t. Every trigger is kept, whatever happened next.
spacing: A trigger counts as an event only if no event occurred in the previous 5 days; later triggers inside that window are ignored.
execution: Entry at the open of day t+1 (the first trade after 00:00 UTC following the signal close). Exit at the open of day t+1+H.
holding: Primary H = 3 days. Secondary H = 1 and 7 days (reported, not used for the decision).
outcome: Per event: equal-weight return of all eligible altcoins minus BTC return over the same window, in percentage points, after costs on the alt legs. Also reported: each coin's own excess, and the absolute equal-weight alt return (vs holding cash).
baselines: (a) Random non-event days: for each event, 20 days drawn from days within +/-30 days of t that are not within 5 days of any event, same execution, universe and costs. (b) Holding BTC: 0 excess, no cost.
splits: Chronological by event: development first 50%, validation next 20%, holdout last 30%, with a 72-hour embargo (events whose window crosses a boundary are dropped). No thresholds are tuned.
inference: Events are at least 5 days apart and H = 3 days, so primary windows do not overlap; 95% CI by bootstrap over events (10,000 resamples). Altcoins in the same event are combined into one portfolio return, so their co-movement is inside each observation.
costs: Labeled cost scenarios (the owner's Kraken fee tier is not available): C1 = 0.8% round trip, C2 = 1.2%, C3 = 2.0%. Context only: Kraken Pro's published taker fee at the lowest volume tier is about 0.40% per side (from memory, not verified against the owner's account). signal.sma: simple average of the last 40 completed weekly closes, including the current week
signal.exit: after the second consecutive completed weekly close below the SMA, move half of the sleeve to cash
signal.re_entry: after the second consecutive completed weekly close above the SMA, restore the full sleeve
signal.state: only two states (full, half); no repeated halving; warm-up 40 weeks before the first signal

The development period contains the 2000-02 and 2008 crashes, so success there is weak evidence; the holdout (2019 onward: 2020 crash, 2022 bear, 2025-26 swings) carries the weight. ETF benchmarks avoid stock-picking hindsight but not the choice of tech as the sleeve.
authority: Research only. A SUPPORTED result does not create a stop, order or deployed Zobiris threshold; adopting the rule needs a separate owner decision.
